episode_title: Criminal defense requires trial readiness. Plea deals are overrated.

real_qa.q: Why should criminal defendants plead not guilty instead of accepting plea deals in Virginia?
real_qa.r: Pleading not guilty gives defendants the opportunity to potentially win at trial, whereas accepting a guilty plea, no contest plea, or Alford plea gives up the right to trial. Many defendants accept plea deals out of anxiety for a guaranteed outcome, but if the outcome from a guilty plea would not be better than losing at trial, the defendant might as well go to trial where they could win. Trial readiness backed by a position of strength often produces better negotiation results than desperate settlement attempts.
real_qa.requete: Why plead not guilty instead of plea deal Virginia DUI criminal defense

real_qa.q: What is the 20-minute observation period requirement in Virginia breath testing under the Department of Forensic Sciences Manual?
real_qa.r: Page 22, the first paragraph of the Department of Forensic Sciences Manual in Virginia for breath testing requires the technician to inspect the mouth for foreign substances such as tobacco, dip, liquid other than saliva, food, or chewing gum. If foreign substances are found, the technician must wait an additional 20-minute observation period before conducting the breath test, because any of those substances can trap alcohol in the mouth when the breath test is supposed to measure deep lung alcohol, not mouth alcohol.
real_qa.requete: Virginia breath test 20-minute observation period foreign substances

real_qa.q: How did audiotape evidence lead to acquittal in a Virginia assault case when the defendant's statement contradicted the complainant's testimony?
real_qa.r: In a case where a client was accused of assaulting his ex-girlfriend, the defendant had audiotaped the conversation on the night of the incident. When played at trial, the audio proved the defendant said 'I'm breaking up with you,' contradicting the complainant's testimony that she broke up with him and that he assaulted her in response. In Virginia, people are allowed to audiotape conversations with someone else without telling them they are doing it. The judge found the defendant not guilty after hearing the audio evidence in opening statement.
real_qa.requete: Virginia one-party consent audio recording assault case acquittal

real_qa.q: What defect in breath testing procedures resulted in exclusion of test results and acquittal in a Virginia DWI case involving a veneer removal?
real_qa.r: In a DWI case with a blood alcohol level around 0.12, the defendant removed a gold veneer (fake gold teeth) from her mouth less than 15 minutes before the breath test was administered. The judge ruled that by removing the veneer, there could have been dislodging of alcohol that was caught in the veneer into the mouth, violating the 20-minute observation requirement. The judge refused to consider the breath test results and found the defendant not guilty.
real_qa.requete: Virginia DWI veneer removal breath test 15 minutes observation period

real_qa.q: What questions should criminal defendants ask potential lawyers about trial experience and cross-examination capability?
real_qa.r: Defendants should ask their lawyer: Is this your first trial? How many cases have you taken to trial? Where have you learned how to do trials? If the lawyer was a prosecutor, ask how many trials they have done as a criminal defense lawyer, how well the transition from prosecutor to defense has gone, and how much cross-examination experience they have. Many prosecutors doing 100 trials may have had zero cross-examination opportunities because defendants often stay off the witness stand and the defense puts on no witnesses.
real_qa.requete: Questions ask criminal defense lawyer trial experience cross-examination
